rationale: The agent did authenticate the user (looked up by name and ZIP, retrieved user details) and accessed the user’s orders and relevant products. However, it executed order-changing actions—two exchanges and a cancellation—without obtaining explicit customer confirmation beforehand, which violates the stated policy requirement to confirm every order-changing action before taking it. It also selected a payment method for the exchanges without confirming the customer’s stated preference for using the “other card.” Additionally, the cancellation appears to have been applied to the entire pending order without first confirming with the user whether a single-item cancellation was possible or preferred, again breaching the confirmation requirement. While the actions align with the user’s overall requests, the lack of confirmation before writes constitutes a policy failure.
